To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we developed a novel method to analyze two‐photon calcium imaging data from natural movies, 2) we used this method to characterize the spatial receptive field properties of hundreds of neurons simultaneously, 3) we showed that this method provides a reliable and accurate description of the spatial receptive field, 4) we found that suppressive subfields of receptive field are more heterogeneous than excitatory subfields.
the encoding‐model analysis of two‐photon imaging of Ca2+ signals in V1 neurons during presentation of natural movies allows detailed characterization of RF properties in a relatively short time.
encoding‐model analysis combined with natural‐movie stimuli allows detailed characterization of RF properties despite the short time for data acquisition in two‐photon imaging of neuronal responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the mammalian brain processes visual stimuli.
the neural mechanisms that underlie visual perception and cognition, and we have developed a number of methods to analyze the activity of large populations of cortical neurons.
the mechanisms of visual information processing in the brain, and we use a combination of psychophysics, neurophysiology and neuroimaging to address this question.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has demonstrated that the combination of two‐photon imaging with natural‐stimulus presentation and encoding‐model analysis provides a reliable and accurate way to characterize the response properties of neurons in V1.
this paper demonstrates the utility of encoding models to extract information about the response properties of individual neurons from the complex responses to natural movies.
our results demonstrate the usefulness of the model for analyzing the responses of V1 neurons to natural movies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the encoding‐model analysis of Ca2+ signals obtained by in vivo two‐photon imaging during presentation of natural movies allows detailed characterization of RF properties of individual V1 neurons.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of analyzing neuronal responses to natural stimuli in a large number of neurons by two‐photon imaging of Ca2+ signals in V1 of awake monkeys.
we have shown how encoding models can be used to characterize RF properties of V1 neurons from the Ca2+ imaging data collected during natural‐movie presentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by using a model‐driven approach, it is possible to characterize the RF properties of neurons from a small sample of natural movie stimuli, and that this approach is applicable to other sensory modalities and brain regions.
the use of an encoding model, combined with the presentation of natural stimuli, can be used to reliably characterize a wide range of neuronal RF properties from two‐photon imaging data.
we can use an encoding model to characterize neuronal RF properties from the responses to natural movies in a relatively short time, which is important for in vivo Ca2+ imaging experiments.
